title: Separate compactification normal forms for the two triple product composites
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p_0,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_{p_0^a}$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, $n\geq1$, and a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with the specified canonical transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes and arrows below are separated and of finite type over $k$; all inputs lie in the displayed bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. Integral pullback and tensor are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite coefficient fields. For any $u:U\to B$, $v:V\to B$ with projections $\pi_U,\pi_V$ on $U\times_BV$, write $u\times_Bv=u\pi_U=v\pi_V$, $P\boxtimes Q=L\pi_U^*P\otimes^L_\Lambda L\pi_V^*Q$, and define the specified morphism
$$\lambda_{u,v}(P,Q)=\alpha_{v,\pi_V}\circ Rv_!\bigl(\operatorname{PF}_{\pi_V,L\pi_U^*P,Q}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{u,v}(P)\otimes1_Q)\bigr)\circ\Psi_v(Ru_!P,Q),$$
where $\Psi_v(F,Q)=Rv_!(\sigma_{Q,Lv^*F})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{v,Q,F}\circ\sigma_{F,Rv_!Q}$ and $\alpha$ is the supplied compact-support compositor. Let $f_i:X_i\to B$ and $K_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,\Lambda)$ for $i=1,2,3$, and choose compactifications $f_i=a_i j_i$ with open $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow\bar X_i$ and proper $a_i:\bar X_i\to B$. Put $P_i=j_{i!}K_i$, $V=X_1\times_BX_2\times_BX_3$, $\bar V=\bar X_1\times_B\bar X_2\times_B\bar X_3$, $u=j_1\times_Bj_2\times_Bj_3$, and $c:\bar V\to B$. Define $\Theta_L(f;K)=\lambda_{f_1\times_Bf_2,f_3}(K_1\boxtimes K_2,K_3)\circ(\lambda_{f_1,f_2}(K_1,K_2)\otimes1)$ and $\Theta_R(f;K)=\lambda_{f_1,f_2\times_Bf_3}(K_1,K_2\boxtimes K_3)\circ(1\otimes\lambda_{f_2,f_3}(K_2,K_3))$. Define $\Theta_L(a;P),\Theta_R(a;P)$ by the same formulas on the proper compactifications.

For two opens $j,k$ over $B$, let $e_{j,k}:(j_!K)\boxtimes(k_!L)\to(j\times_Bk)_!(K\boxtimes L)$ be the normalized open external tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-external-tensor-normalization] at finite coefficients, and its completed, rationalized and common-stage forms of [lem-sf-integral-open-product-diagram-normalization] at the other stages. On $\bar V$, set
$$e_L=e_{j_1\times j_2,j_3}\circ(e_{j_1,j_2}\boxtimes1),\qquad
e_R=e_{j_1,j_2\times j_3}\circ(1\boxtimes e_{j_2,j_3}),$$
with extension-by-zero composition and tensor associators inserted. These are isomorphisms from $P_1\boxtimes P_2\boxtimes P_3$ to $u_!(K_1\boxtimes K_2\boxtimes K_3)$, restrict to the identity on $V$, and satisfy $e_L=e_R$ under the associators. Under the specified compactification comparisons for all input and output direct images, the two separate normal-form identities hold:
$$\Theta_L(f;K)=Rc_*(e_L)\circ\Theta_L(a;P),\qquad
\Theta_R(f;K)=Rc_*(e_R)\circ\Theta_R(a;P).$$
All displayed comparisons respect refinement of the chosen compactifications. At integral coefficients the comparisons are images under functorial $R\lim$ of morphisms and equalities in the derived category of the actual strict finite-reduction diagrams, with derived pointwise tensor over $m\mapsto A_{E,m}$. Their finite reductions are bounded constructible with bounded etale-origin witnesses, without requiring transition maps between the witnesses. At field stages the equalities use rationalization and scalar extension from a common finite field. No injectivity of reduction on integral derived Hom sets is part of this assertion.

source.place: Reduction to proper f,g in the symmetry paragraph, extended to three factors for clause (ii): returned steps 5--8, including coefficient passage in the derived strict-diagram category.

proof.text: First take $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. For $ij=12,23$, put $X_{ij}=X_i\times_BX_j$, $\bar X_{ij}=\bar X_i\times_B\bar X_j$, $j_{ij}=j_i\times_Bj_j$, $a_{ij}:\bar X_{ij}\to B$, $D_{ij}=K_i\boxtimes K_j$, $Q_{ij}=P_i\boxtimes P_j$ and $H_{ij}=j_{ij!}D_{ij}$. The maps $a_{ij}$ and $c$ are proper: each is a composite of base changes of the $a_i$. The product opens are the open subschemes obtained by intersecting the inverse images of the $X_i\subset\bar X_i$ under the product projections; hence $j_{ij}$ and $u$ are open immersions. The required complexes are in the finite-Tor constructible domains: open extension preserves the input intervals, pullback preserves them, and tensor adds the two Tor intervals. Bounded constructible inputs have bounded etale-origin witnesses, so the compactification comparisons apply.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text:
Write $e_{ij}:Q_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{ij}$ for the normalized binary open comparison. Apply the binary compactification identity to $(f_i,f_j)$, using precisely $a_i j_i,a_j j_j$. In compactification coordinates this gives
$$\lambda_{f_i,f_j}(K_i,K_j)=Ra_{ij*}(e_{ij})\,\lambda_{a_i,a_j}(P_i,P_j).$$
The same identity applies to $(f_1\times_Bf_2,f_3)$ using $a_{12}j_{12},a_3j_3$, and to $(f_1,f_2\times_Bf_3)$ using $a_1j_1,a_{23}j_{23}$. Thus its outer proper inputs are respectively $(H_{12},P_3)$ and $(P_1,H_{23})$.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text:
The proper comparison $\lambda_{a,b}$ is natural in both inputs. Indeed its defining factors are natural transformations: exchange, projection, the signed symmetry, and the direct-image compositor. Composing their naturality squares gives, for $s:C\to C'$ on the source of $a$ and $t:N\to N'$ on the source of $b$,
$$\lambda_{a,b}(C',N')\,(Ra_*s\otimes Rb_*t)
=R(a\times_Bb)_*(s\boxtimes t)\,\lambda_{a,b}(C,N).$$
Here $a,b$ are proper, so the proper identifications of the supplied six-functor datum identify the shriek factors with these star factors. This argument asserts naturality only; it uses no triple-product coherence theorem.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text:
For the left parenthesization, substitute the $ij=12$ equality of step 2 into the inner factor, and its outer equality into the outer factor. In the resulting composite the middle part is
$$\lambda_{a_{12},a_3}(H_{12},P_3)\,(Ra_{12*}e_{12}\otimes1).$$
Step 3 with $s=e_{12}$ and $t=1$ replaces this by
$$Rc_*(e_{12}\boxtimes1)\,\lambda_{a_{12},a_3}(Q_{12},P_3).$$
Consequently
$$\Theta_L(f;K)=Rc_*\!\left(e_{j_{12},j_3}\,(e_{12}\boxtimes1)\right)\Theta_L(a;P)=Rc_*(e_L)\Theta_L(a;P).$$
Functoriality of $Rc_*$ combines the two displayed output maps. The extension-composition and fibre-product identifications in this calculation are the supplied compactification ones; their associativity is clause (A4).

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text:
For the right parenthesization substitute the $ij=23$ and the corresponding outer equalities of step 2. Its middle part becomes
$$\lambda_{a_1,a_{23}}(P_1,H_{23})\,(1\otimes Ra_{23*}e_{23}).$$
Step 3 with $s=1$ and $t=e_{23}$ gives
$$Rc_*(1\boxtimes e_{23})\,\lambda_{a_1,a_{23}}(P_1,Q_{23}).$$
Therefore
$$\Theta_R(f;K)=Rc_*\!\left(e_{j_1,j_{23}}\,(1\boxtimes e_{23})\right)\Theta_R(a;P)=Rc_*(e_R)\Theta_R(a;P).$$
This calculation establishes the right normal form separately; it does not identify the two proper triple composites.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: The binary open maps are isomorphisms and restrict to identity. Apply their three-open associativity clause to $j_1,j_2,j_3$. It says exactly that $e_L=e_R$, with the normalized extension compositors inserted, and that both restrictions are identity on $K_1\boxtimes K_2\boxtimes K_3$. Pullback monoidality, including its associativity compatibility, identifies the nested external products used in steps 4 and 5 with the displayed triple products. Thus their sources and targets are precisely those in the item.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: The finite binary identity is compatible with refinement of each chosen compactification. Apply its refinement squares to the two applications in step 2 for either parenthesization. The exchange factors commute with these comparisons, and the projection factors are independent of compactification through these comparisons. Whisker these commuting squares by the remaining factors and paste them. Their common middle comparisons cancel, so the entire left and right normal-form squares commute. The open associativity identity is between the same normalized maps already appearing in these squares; it introduces no choice of an additional comparison.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: Now take $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. Work with the actual strict reduction diagrams $K_{i,\bullet}$ over $m\mapsto A_{E,m}$ and their derived pointwise tensor. The integral open-product diagram theorem supplies $e^\bullet_{ij}$ and the binary compactification identity as actual morphisms and equalities in the derived diagram category, together with its three-open associativity equality. Apply that theorem four times, to $(1,2),(2,3),(12,3),(1,23)$, using the same product compactifications as step 2. It also supplies the bounded constructible finite reductions and bounded etale-origin witnesses for these expressions. Only the actual diagrams carry transitions; the witnesses at different $m$ need not do so.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: In that derived diagram category repeat the substitutions of steps 4 and 5. Naturality of the diagram exchange/projection composite follows by composing the naturality squares of its canonical factors, just as in step 3; these are actual system transformations, with their canonical pullback/tensor and direct-image compositors. Thus the middle maps are respectively $R_c^{\mathcal T}(e_{12}^\bullet\boxtimes1)$ and $R_c^{\mathcal T}(1\boxtimes e_{23}^\bullet)$. Composing with the two outer open maps gives the diagram versions of $e_L$ and $e_R$. They agree by the diagram associativity clause. This proves both normal-form equalities before any evaluation or limit is taken. Its realization hypotheses hold for the finitely many expressions here: integral finite Tor amplitude supplies intervals independent of $m$; open extension preserves them and tensor adds them, as in step 1. Each proper source has finite dimension $d$, so etale direct-image vanishing gives the uniform bound $2d$, and the direct-image Tor theorem gives $[a,b+2d]$ for every $m$. Use $d=0$ for an empty source. The operation/reduction comparisons give normalized transitions. If a coherent etale presentation is needed, apply the derived system comparison to the actual reduction system: its counit supplies that presentation since every level has bounded etale origin. It does not require transitions on the witnesses originally chosen. For the coefficient hypotheses, the DVR theorem gives $0<|\varpi_E|<1$ and a non-zero-divisor $\varpi_E$. Representatives of compatible residue classes are Cauchy, since successive differences lie in $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_E$. Completeness of $E$ gives a limit in the closed unit ball $\mathcal O_E$ representing every residue class. Injectivity follows from $|\varpi_E|^m\to0$. Thus $\mathcal O_E\cong\lim_m A_{E,m}$. These verify the coefficient hypotheses of that comparison.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: Apply functorial $R\lim$ to these diagram maps and equalities. The open-product diagram theorem identifies the binary maps with the required completed $e$, exchange/PF composites and their compactification comparisons. The system-realization theorem intertwines all their whiskerings, including nested compact-support and tensor expressions, with the completed operations. Therefore the limits of the two equations in step 9 are exactly the two integral normal forms, and the limit of the diagram open associativity equality is $e_L=e_R$. A functor preserves identities and isomorphisms, giving the remaining open normalization assertions. This uses images of already equal diagram arrows, not injectivity of finite reduction on any integral Hom set.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: For integral refinement, the normalized proper/open comparison satisfies its horizontal, vertical and base-change pasting equations in the derived strict-tower category, including refinement squares. Its semilinear realization satisfies these equations before scalar restriction or evaluation. The refinement squares for exchange commute by the refinement clause of the exchange theorem; those for projection commute by independence of compactification in projection coherence. Paste the binary squares as in step 7 and apply their contextual realization comparisons and $R\lim$. This gives the refinement squares of both completed normal forms, with the prescribed compactification maps.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof.text: For $E$-coefficients apply rationalization to the integral equations. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ choose a common finite coefficient field representing the finite list of inputs and maps, and apply its scalar-extension functor. The open-product coefficient theorem identifies these images with the prescribed open and binary compactification maps. Operation/coefficient comparisons preserve the tensor associators, units, counits and hence the ordered composites defining $\Theta_L$ and $\Theta_R$. Functoriality carries both normal forms, open associativity and the refinement squares to the field stages. The scalar-extension cocycle makes their classes independent of enlarging the common field. No reduction of rational coefficients to $A_{E,m}$ is used.

source.place: Triple-product clause (ii), compactification reduction and naturality of the specified binary composite

proof_origin.place: Explicit double application of the binary compactification normal form in the reduction-to-proper paragraph and triple-product clause (ii).
